title: Formalisme algébrique des correspondances et algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge (cf conjectures standard) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), lettres (1966-1967).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a typescript page numbered 42, with handwritten corrections. It is not part of the 'Poincaré–Hodge algebra' notes around it. It is a draft of the ℓ-adic section of 'Le groupe de Brauer III' (Dix exposés, 1968). The neighbouring pages are handwritten computations with Lefschetz operators L and Λ, and the show-through on this sheet suggests its back was used as scrap paper for them.

Standing assumption (presumably stated on the previous typescript page): H^i(X, Z/ℓ) is finite. Then H^i(X, μ_{ℓ^∞}) is of cofinite type, i.e. its maximal divisible subgroup (Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ)^r plus a finite group.

Step 1, sequence (8.3). Take the sequence 0 → μ_{ℓ^ν} → μ_{ℓ^∞} --(ℓ^ν)--> μ_{ℓ^∞} → 0. Its long exact sequence gives 0 → H^{i-1}(μ_{ℓ^∞})/ℓ^ν → H^i(μ_{ℓ^ν}) → H^i(μ_{ℓ^∞})[ℓ^ν] → 0.
- On the left, the divisible part is killed, so for large ν the term stabilises at t^{i-1}(X,ℓ) = H^{i-1}/(H^{i-1})°, where ° denotes the maximal divisible subgroup. This is a finite ℓ-group, so the Mittag-Leffler condition holds.
- Passing to the limit gives 0 → t^{i-1} → H^i(X, Z_ℓ(1)) → T_ℓ H^i(X, μ_{ℓ^∞}) → 0.
- Since T_ℓ is torsion-free, t^{i-1} is the torsion submodule of the finitely generated Z_ℓ-module H^i(X, Z_ℓ(1)), and the free quotient is T_ℓ H^i.

Step 2, isomorphism (8.6). (H^i(μ_{ℓ^∞}))° ≅ H^i(Z_ℓ(1)) ⊗ Q_ℓ / image of H^i(Z_ℓ(1)). Hence torsion ℓ-adic cohomology and integral ℓ-adic cohomology determine each other modulo finite groups.

Step 3, sequence (8.7). Assume Pic X is an extension of a finitely generated NS(X) by a divisible group, and H^2(X, Z/ℓ) is finite. Apply the same limit to the Kummer sequences 0 → Pic/ℓ^ν → H^2(μ_{ℓ^ν}) → Br'[ℓ^ν] → 0. This gives 0 → NS ⊗ Z_ℓ → H^2(X, Z_ℓ(1)) → T_ℓ Br'(X) → 0.
- Corollary: (NS)_tors{ℓ} ≅ H^2(X, Z_ℓ(1))_tors, an ℓ-adic analogue of the transcendental fact. The handwritten correction to 'ℓ-primary component' is needed for this to be true.
- T_ℓ Br' is thereby identified with the 'transcendental part' of H^2.

Step 4, start of the next topic. For X a proper smooth connected surface over an algebraically closed field (the word 'surface' is added by hand), consider the cup-product symmetric bilinear form on H^2(X, Z_ℓ(1)), with values in H^4(X, Z_ℓ(2)) ≅ Z_ℓ. This leads, in the published text, to comparing discriminants of NS and H^2 and to the Artin–Tate circle of ideas.
errors: No mathematical errors in the final corrected text.

The typed original said the whole torsion subgroup of NS(X) is isomorphic to the torsion of H^2(X, Z_ℓ(1)). This is false (the prime-to-ℓ torsion is lost), and Grothendieck corrected it by hand to 'la composante ℓ-primaire'.
The bilinear-form statement needs X to be a surface (or else middle degree); this was also added by hand.
The finiteness hypothesis on H^i(X, Z/ℓ) used for (8.3)–(8.6) is not visible on this page; presumably it is on the preceding typescript page.
(8.6) is canonical only when read as the image of H^i(Z_ℓ(1)) ⊗ Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ, which is fine.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft typescript page of the published 'Le groupe de Brauer III' §8, apparently reused as scrap paper for the Lefschetz-algebra notes. Its content is published and well known. The only minor archival interest is the visible hand-corrections (ℓ-primary component, 'surface', notation Z_ℓ[1] for the Tate twist).
transcription_corrections: In the handwritten insertion the definition is Z_ℓ[1] = lim_ν μ_{ℓ^ν} ('faisceau ℓ-adique de TATE'), with the inverse limit over ν.
(8.5) right-hand side is lim H^i(X, μ_{ℓ^ν}) (handwritten μ_{ℓ^ν}).
The leading symbol in (8.6) is struck out; the left-hand side is H^i(X, μ_{ℓ^∞})°, so the transcription's unmatched opening parenthesis should be dropped.
'mod groupes [-...-] finis' has a struck word (probably 'tous' or similar) before 'finis'.
The page bears typescript number 42 (top right) and archive number 20 (bottom left).
